our_interpretation: Read as a claim about legal accountability already imposed by March 29, 2024, rather than a forecast about subsequent cases.

The ordinary test is whether a court or regulator had imposed liability or a binding remedy on a generative AI provider for harm caused by its generated content. Pending complaints and investigations do not establish liability.
Include copyright harm because the immediately preceding passage discusses harm to artists and creators.

Read the unqualified reference to companies as including commercial generative AI service providers across jurisdictions. The surrounding references to Congress, Microsoft and OpenAI also permit a narrower reading focused on major US developers.
The target period is cumulative legal history through publication. No starting date or regular reporting period is supplied; the latest observable legal status is the status on March 29, 2024.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable, sufficiently comprehensive legal records establish that no in-scope provider had been held liable or subjected to a binding remedy for harm caused by generated content by March 29, 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one court judgment or regulatory disposition effective by March 29, 2024 imposed liability or a binding remedy on an in-scope provider for harm caused by generated content.
